extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, and students of stand-up comedy
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting descriptive criteria and techniques used in Stewart Lee's stand-up (style, subject matter, delivery, and career choices) useful for evaluating or producing similar alternative/comedic work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition, internal reference, and deadpan delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Stewart Lee's stand-up routine is characterised by repetition, internal reference, and deadpan delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are core stylistic markers: repeat motifs and callbacks (internal reference) to build texture and expectation; use deadpan delivery to contrast content and tone. Combined they create a recognisable comedic voice and pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter: topical, observational, self-deprecating, absurd
rubrics_metrics.description: His comedy covers a wide range of forms and subject material. It is often topical, observational, self-deprecating and absurd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose subject matter that can be topical or observational, mixing self-deprecation and absurdity. Variety in forms (sketch, stand-up, satire) is acceptable; coherence comes from consistent voice and thematic through-lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tackling controversial themes (religion, political correctness, artistic integrity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notable routines have focused on topics like religion, political correctness and artistic integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engaging with morally or politically charged subjects is a deliberate choice; expect backlash. Use rigorous framing and intent to defend material, and be prepared for public controversy and discourse about offence vs. provocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-humour and explicit structure disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: He employs meta-humour, openly describing the structure and intent of the set while onstage, and abolishing the illusion of his routines as spontaneous acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the audience aware of the mechanics of the act (tease, reveal, misdirection) to create a second-order comic effect. Anti-pattern: pretending spontaneity when the bit depends on its artifice—Lee instead foregrounds artifice as part of the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pull back and reveal technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique of concealing the true subject of a joke until the last moment, a method he labelled 'pull back and reveal'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure jokes so that the apparent subject is subverted at the punch moment. Note: this technique often relies on language-specific ambiguity and can be difficult to translate; it demands precise timing and control of audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write about ideas for translatability (avoid language-dependent crutches)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandoned writing jokes in a traditional sense, instead focusing on writing humorous material about ideas which would be more easily translatable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating material intended for non-native-language contexts, prefer concept-driven humour over wordplay/puns. Lee's experience in Germany led him to 'kick away comedy crutches' and focus on idea-based comedy that survives translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of onstage personae and ironic alternation
rubrics_metrics.description: Delivery uses onstage personae, frequently alternating between that of an outspoken left-wing hero and that of a depressed failure and champagne socialist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt and switch between exaggerated personae to create dramatic irony and layered critique. This allows the performer to inhabit contradictory stances and satirise both targets and the performer themself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scolding or mocking the audience as a device
rubrics_metrics.description: He often criticises the audience for not being intelligent enough to understand his jokes, saying they would prefer more simplistic material, or enjoy mainstream 'arena' comedians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directly addressing and mocking audience tastes (e.g., 'liberal intelligentsia') can be used to set a confrontational tone and to filter the crowd. Anti-pattern: overuse risks alienation and collapse of rapport if not calibrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culmination in feigned depressive episodes / nervous breakdowns
rubrics_metrics.description: His routines often culminate in feigned depressive episodes and nervous breakdowns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a staged collapse or emotional breakdown as a climax can puncture expectations and produce darkly comic effects. Requires careful control to avoid genuine distress or misinterpretation; it's a high-risk, high-reward tactic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provocation to expose hypocrisy (operating between provocation and offence)
rubrics_metrics.description: He 'operates out in that dangerous hinterland between moral provocation and outright offence, often adopting, as in this instance, the tactics of those he targets in order to highlight their hypocrisy'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the rhetoric/techniques of an opponent to mirror and expose contradictions; intended effect is critical illumination rather than endorsement. Be aware of public reactions and be prepared to contextualise the provocation to avoid being read as endorsing harmful views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using negative criticism as audience-filtering marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: He frequently uses negative reviews on his posters to put off potential audience members who are unlikely to like his comedy style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reframe bad reviews as a marketing tool to target the desired audience and deter mismatched ticket-buyers. This tactic leverages niche positioning over mass appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career-choice principle: avoid mainstream quick-money appearances to preserve integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Lee decided to quit comedy panel shows and said he did not want to alienate his audience in exchange for quick money by such appearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing not to pursue certain mainstream gigs (panel shows, easy TV spots) can be a deliberate career/brand decision to maintain credibility with a particular audience. Trade-off: slower financial returns versus sustained artistic identity.
